full_text_zh:
[P1] 西游记之廿一
真假孙悟空

[P2] 真假孙悟空
《西游记》之二十一
原著 吴承恩
改编 陈平夫
绘画 宋静风
周静秋
河北美术出版社
内容提要
这本画册是根据古典文学名著《西游记》第五十六回——
五十八回改编的。故事叙述唐僧师徒四人，在西天取经途中，孙悟空因杀死强盗，反被师父驱走。山中有一妖猴趁
机变作悟空模样，抢走唐僧的行李、关文。悟空在如来帮助下杀死了妖猴，和师父重归于好，又奔西天取经去了。

[P3] 1  唐僧师徒西天取经，来到一座山前，忽然一阵喧闹，从山腰里跑来一群小猴，它们有的模仿拖棒，有的模仿扛钯，有的模仿挑担，还有的跳上唐僧骑的白龙马乱抓乱搔。
2  白龙马被抓搔得撒腿就跑，那群猴在后面紧追。只累得一个个气喘吁吁，惹得八戒捧腹大笑，拉住悟空叫道：‘猴哥你看，这都是你的子孙后代，多好玩啊！’

[P4] 3 惊马难收。那马出了山口，又跑了二十多里，多亏松林拦路，唐僧这才挽住缰绳。
4 唐僧刚喘了口气，忽听一阵锣响，从松林里拥出一伙贼人，拦住马头叫道：‘留下买路银子放你过去，若说半个不字，管叫你的秃头搬家！’

[P5] 5 唐僧吓得哀求道:“贫僧是东土唐王差往西天取经的，沿路乞食化斋，哪来的银子孝敬大王，还求大王行个方便，放我过去吧!”
6 贼头听了，举棍要打。唐僧一看势头不好，只得扯谎说:“大王别打，银子在我徒弟身上，他在后边就来了。”那贼头喝道:“先把他绑起来!”众喽罗把唐僧绑好，吊在树上。

[P6] 7 不大一会儿，悟空他们赶来了，八戒老远便喊：‘你们来看呀，师父等急了，正爬在树上瞅我们呢。’
8 悟空仔细一看，说：‘呆子，那是师父被贼人吊在树上，你们慢来，等我先去看看。’好大圣，摇身一变，变了个小和尚，背着一个蓝布包袱，向前走去。

[P7] 9 悟空走到唐僧跟前。那伙贼人围拢过来，说：‘小和尚，你师父说，银子在你包袱里，快取出来，饶你两个的性命！’
10 悟空放下包袱说：‘大王别嚷，银子只有百十两，黄金倒有几十锭，只要先把我师父放下来，我便连包袱都送给你们。’那贼头一听，便吩咐喽罗放下唐僧。

[P8] 11 悟空用手向来路一指，对唐僧说：‘师父先走，等我交了银子就去赶你。’唐僧上马跑去了。
12 悟空看师父走远，把包袱一摊说：‘拿过来吧！’那贼头忙问：‘什么呀？’悟空道：‘银子。我背了一路空包袱，把你们劫来的银子分些与我做盘缠吧！’

[P9] 13 贼头气得直跳，抡起藤棍照悟空头上就打，一连打了几十下，累得臂酸手疼，那悟空却把眼一翻笑道：‘再来几下嘛，痒丝丝的怪好受哩。’
14 那伙贼人不知悟空的厉害，一个个拿刀端枪，一拥而上。悟空恼怒，取出金箍棒，左右一挑，就把两个贼头甩到半空，吓得众喽罗全跑光了。

[P10] 15 这时，唐僧和八戒、沙僧走过来。唐僧问贼人哪儿去了？悟空道：‘喽罗散了，两个贼头一个被我扔进北海，一个送到南山去了。’
16 当日晚上，唐僧师徒赶到一个村庄借宿。一个姓杨的老汉很热情地把他们让到家里。

[P11] 17 半夜里，唐僧师徒睡得正香，忽然一伙贼人闯了进来，他们正是在松林里惊散了的贼人。贼人中有个是杨老汉的儿子，他们一看唐僧师徒住在这里，便忙着磨刀擦枪，要杀唐僧师徒。
18 杨老汉是个好心人，他痛恨这伙贼人不务正业，可又管教不了儿子。杨老汉见此情景，悄悄地忙来给唐僧送信，并领他们从后门逃走。

[P12] 19 唐僧师徒刚走不远，就听后面一片喊嚷。唐僧回头看，叫道：“不好了，贼人追来了，可怎么办哪？！”
20 悟空对八戒和沙僧说：“你二人保护师父先走，等我收拾他们！”唐僧听了反担心地说：“悟空啊！只吓退他们就行，可别再伤人了。”

[P13] 21 那伙贼人想趁天黑行凶，于是追上来，照准悟空乱砍乱打。悟空为了防身，用棒只一抡，便把那些靠近他的贼人打死了，离得远的吓得东逃西散。
22 唐僧见悟空又打死了人，骂道：‘你这泼猴，把贼人赶跑就够了，为何又杀人！’他说着便下马坐定，把脸一沉，念起紧箍咒来了。咒得悟空眼胀头昏，痛得就地直滚，可唐僧还不住口地念着。

[P14] 23 悟空哀求道：‘师父饶了我吧，别再念了！’唐僧这才住口，说：‘没说的，我不要你了，你回去吧！’
24 悟空跪下道：‘师父，怎的又赶我走？’唐僧说：‘你这泼猴凶恶太甚，不是取经之人。快走！快走！免得又念真言。’悟空也生气了，说了声‘去’，便一个筋斗，无影无踪了。

[P15] 25 悟空在空中暗想：这和尚既然负心，我何不去告诉观音菩萨。想罢便直奔南洋大海去了。
26 悟空到了落伽山，穿过紫竹林，直奔潮音洞，拜见观音菩萨，泪如泉涌，放声大哭。

[P16] 27 菩萨问明原由，对悟空说：‘对待毛贼应好言劝诫；随便打杀，也是你的不对。’悟空心中不平，心想：菩萨为啥也这样不分青红皂白呀？
28 悟空求菩萨解了紧箍咒，放他回山。菩萨说：‘保唐僧取经，才是正理，西天路上，灾难重重，你师父会来寻你，你就住在这里等等吧。’

[P17] 29 再说唐僧撵走了悟空以后，继续西行，走了半天不见村庄，又饥又渴，叫八戒去化斋取水，好久不见八戒回来，又打发沙僧去寻八戒。
30 唐僧刚静下心，闭目养神，就听空中一阵风响，当是八戒回来了，睁眼一看，却是悟空捧了一盂清水站在面前。

[P18] 31 悟空说：‘师父，离了我老孙，别说去西天，你连水也喝不上，这水你先喝了，等我再去化斋。’唐僧喝道：‘我渴死也不喝你的水！你快去，慢走一步，我要念咒了！’
32 悟空听罢破口大骂：‘你这秃和尚，欺我太甚！’说着照准唐僧后背就是一棒。

[P19] 33 唐僧哎呀一声晕倒在地上。那悟空也不理睬，把行李一提驾云走了。
34 不多时，八戒和沙僧化斋回来，见师父倒在地上，白马脱缰，行李不见，大吃一惊。

[P20] 35 沙僧抱起师父直哭，八戒道：‘这一定是那伙没杀净的贼人干的，如今哭有屁用！你守着尸体，等我去把马卖了，换口棺木，埋了师父，你去你的流沙河，我回我的高老庄。’
36 沙僧实在不忍离舍，忙叫八戒给师父灌口水。唐僧咽了几口水，慢慢苏醒，把刚才的事讲给八戒沙僧听。八戒气得咬牙切齿，骂道：‘好你泼猴，竟敢打骂师父，待我老猪找他算账去！’

[P21] 37 沙僧一把拉住八戒说：‘别急，先扶师父到山后村子里，化些热汤吃了，再找个住处，让师父休息调养，那时你再去也不晚呀。’
38 八戒只得依从沙僧，扶师父进了村庄，化些斋饭热汤。唐僧吃了半碗，才觉有些精神，问道：‘谁去讨行李？’

[P22] 39 八戒要去，唐僧想了想说：‘你去不得，你和泼猴素来不和，说话又粗鲁，万一触怒了他，打，你也打不过他，还是悟净去一趟吧。’
40 沙僧临行，唐僧再三叮咛：‘你到那里要见机行事，他给就要，不给，便到菩萨那里去告。千万不要同他翻脸争执，因为你也不是他的对手啊！’沙僧连连答应，跳上云头，奔东胜神州去了。

[P23] 41 沙僧走了三天三夜，过了东洋大海，到了花果山界，按下云头，找到水帘洞，就听群猴唧唧啾啾一片喧嚷。
42 再仔细一看，那孙悟空高坐在石台上，正摇头晃脑地念着“通关文牒”呢。

[P24] 43 沙僧听他念到中途收得大徒弟孙悟空，二徒弟……
忍不住叫道:“师兄，你偷走关文，害得师父不能去西天取经，快把师父急坏了……”
44 那悟空喝道:“你是何人？敢闯进我的仙洞!”沙僧看他翻脸不认人，连忙行礼道:“师兄息怒，师父错怪了你，你若不恨师父，就同我回去，若不回去，千万把行李关文交还小弟……”

[P25] 45 悟空听了冷笑道：‘我打唐僧，抢行李，是我自己要上西方拜佛求经，送上东土，我独成功，教那南赡部州人立我为祖，万代传名也！’
46 沙僧正在发怔，悟空又说：‘你不信呀？待我请来我的唐僧给你看。’只听他一声吆喝，果然从洞里出来唐僧骑着白马，后跟着八戒挑行李，沙僧拿锡杖。

[P26] 47 沙僧一见大怒道：‘我老沙行不更名，坐不改姓，那里又有个沙和尚，妖邪休走，吃我一杖。’手起杖落，打得假沙僧现了原形，原来是个猴精变的。
48 假悟空恼怒，喝令众猴围住沙僧要打。沙僧一纵身，跳上云头，直往南海禀报菩萨去了。

[P27] 49 沙僧到了落伽山，拜见观音菩萨，抬头看见悟空笑嘻嘻地站在一旁，不由一怔，心想：这个泼猴，走到我前面，一定先在菩萨面前颠倒是非了……
50 菩萨正要问话，只见沙僧直眉瞪眼，举起宝杖，照着悟空劈面就打。悟空闪过，沙僧又追，菩萨喝道：‘悟净住手！有话明讲，怎么在我面前动起武来了。’

[P28] 51 沙僧连忙赔罪，接着把前后情由讲了一遍，最后又气冲冲地说：‘是我特来禀告菩萨，不想他赶到了我前面，还望菩萨不要信他的假话呀！’
52 菩萨道：‘悟净，你可不要赖人，悟空在这里已经住了四天了。’沙僧不信，指着悟空直嚷：‘他来去无踪，变化多端，我绝对不会在菩萨面前撒谎呀！’

[P29] 53 菩萨见沙僧急得面红耳赤，便说：‘既如此，你休发怒，叫悟空与你同去花果山看看。到那里自见分晓。’
54 悟空、沙僧辞别菩萨，出了洞口，沙僧一把拉住悟空说：‘这一回咱两个得一起走，你别再藏头露尾了。’悟空答应，二人一同驾云而去。

[P30] 55 到了花果山，沙僧先看见那个“孙悟空”，便指给悟空：“师兄你看，那石台上坐的是谁？！”
56 悟空一看大怒，一个纵身跳到洞前喝道：“哪来的妖邪，竟敢变我相貌，占我仙洞，骗我子孙，吃我一棒！”

[P31] 57 那个悟空也不答话，举棒相迎，二条金箍棒上下翻滚，同样好武艺，难解难分。
58 弄得沙僧难分真假，喊了声师兄，两个一齐答应：想帮手，又怕伤了真的。正在纳闷，就听一个叫道：“沙僧，你先回去禀复师父，待我与此妖打到菩萨那里辨个真假。”

[P32] 59 沙僧听了，认定这个是真的。可是，那个也一字不差地说了一遍，马上又把他弄糊涂了。沙僧心想：帮不得手，待我先去取行李来。
60 可是，他跑回洞口却找不到行李。这时，两个悟空也打得不知去向，自己只得离开花果山，回禀师父去了。

[P33] 61 两个悟空打到落伽山，见了观音菩萨，这个说：‘我是真的。’那个说：‘他是假的。’争吵不休。
62 菩萨看不出真假。心想：暗念紧箍咒，看哪个怕疼，哪个便是真的。没料到一念咒，两个都抱着头就地打滚，疼得齐喊‘饶命！’

[P34] 63 念咒不灵。菩萨喊悟空，两个都答应。菩萨说：‘两个总有一个是假的，你跟随师父多年，快去求他辨个真假吧。’
64 却说那沙僧从花果山回来，对师父一讲，唐僧又悔又怕地说：‘是我错怪了悟空，可这妖怪神通广大，万一悟空也斗他不过，丢了关文行李，我们怎么去西天取经呀？’

[P35] 65 师徒三人正在议论，就听空中一阵吵嚷，连忙出来一看，却是两个悟空打打骂骂地来了。
66 八戒等不及他们下来，便纵身跳起，叫道：‘待我老猪去看看哪个猴头是真的。’

[P36] 67 八戒到了空中，一叫师兄，两个一齐答应道：‘兄弟来得正好，快帮我打妖精吧！’八戒瞧瞧这个，又看看那个，难辨真假，便上前一手扯住一个说：‘走，见师父去。’
68 唐僧见了两个悟空，也认不出真假，念咒也不灵。后来想出个主意说：‘悟空会七十二变，我说什么，谁会变，谁就是真的。’

[P37] 69 唐僧说:“公鸡!”一眨眼工夫，面前就是两只一模一样的大公鸡，在伸颈长鸣。
70 唐僧说:“蟋蟀!”又一眨眼工夫，面前便是一对一般大小的蟋蟀，在震须格斗。

[P38] 71 说什么，他们变什么。急得唐僧没法，便说：‘谁敢到雷音寺去见如来佛，谁就是真的。’两个悟空听了，拉拉扯扯，同驾云雾，真的打上西天去了。
72 两个悟空去后，唐僧连忙吩咐八戒道：‘你趁他不在花果山，快去找回行李，我们也好赶路，不管它谁真谁假，反正我也不指望用他了。’

[P39] 73 却说如来佛正在讲经说法，只见跑来两个悟空，都求他辨个真假。如来仔细一看，用手指着那假悟空道：‘好你大胆的六耳猕猴，竟骗到我跟前来了。’
74 那假悟空一听如来说出自己的本相，吓得胆战心惊，正想逃走，早被众神团团围住。

[P40] 75 假悟空忙把身子一摇，变了个蜜蜂儿想逃走，却被如来的金钵罩住，立刻现了原形。
76 悟空怒火难消，忍不住一棒打下去，结果了六耳猕猴的性命。

[P41] 77 正在这时，菩萨来了。如来说保唐僧西天取经是正道，并叫菩萨带悟空去见唐僧。
78 悟空跟随菩萨见了唐僧，把话说开，师徒和好如初，正好八戒也背着行李从花果山回来。菩萨回转南海，唐僧师徒四人，欢欢喜喜地又上路西行了。要知后事如何，请看《三盗芭蕉扇》。

[P1] Journey to the West Chapter Twenty-One
The Real and Fake Sun Wukong

[P2] The Real and Fake Monkey King
Chapter Twenty-One of "Journey to the West"
Original Author: Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by: Chen Pingfu
Illustrated by: Song Jingfeng
Zhou Jingqiu
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House
Synopsis
This picture book is adapted from chapters fifty-six to fifty-eight of the classical literary masterpiece "Journey to the West". The story narrates how, during their journey to the West to obtain scriptures, the four disciples of Tang Sanzang, Sun Wukong was driven away by his master after killing bandits. A demon monkey in the mountains took the opportunity to transform into Wukong's likeness, stealing Tang Sanzang's luggage and official documents. With the help of Buddha, Wukong killed the demon monkey, reconciled with his master, and resumed their journey to the West to obtain the scriptures.

[P3] 1  Tang Monk and his disciples were traveling west to fetch scriptures. They arrived at the foot of a mountain when suddenly a commotion erupted. A group of little monkeys came running out from the mountain's midsection. Some imitated dragging a staff, some imitated carrying a rake, some imitated shouldering a load, and others jumped onto the White Dragon Horse that Tang Monk was riding, scratching and pulling at it.
2  The White Dragon Horse, scratched and pulled, ran off at full speed, with the monkeys chasing after it. The monkeys were exhausted, panting heavily. This amused Bajie, who burst out laughing, grabbed Wukong, and called out: 'Brother Monkey, look! These are all your descendants. How fun!'

[P4] 3 The frightened horse was hard to control. After leaving the mountain pass, it ran more than twenty miles. Fortunately, the pine forest blocked the way, and Tang Sanzang was finally able to pull on the reins.
4 Just as Tang Sanzang caught his breath, he suddenly heard the sound of gongs. A group of bandits burst out from the pine forest, blocking the horse's path and shouting: 'Leave your toll money and we'll let you pass. If you say even half a word of no, we'll make your bald head move house!'

[P5] 5 The monk trembled and pleaded: "I am a monk sent by Emperor Tang of the Eastern Land to fetch scriptures from the West. I beg for alms along the way. Where would I get silver to offer to you, Your Majesty? I beg you to spare me and let me pass!"
6 The bandit chief, upon hearing this, raised his club to strike. Seeing the situation was dire, the monk lied: "Your Majesty, don't hit me! The silver is with my disciple. He's coming right behind me!" The bandit chief roared: "Bind him first!" The bandits tied up the monk and hung him from a tree.

[P6] 7 Not long after, Wukong and the others arrived. Bajie shouted from afar: 'Come and see! Master is waiting anxiously, climbing up the tree and looking at us.'
8 Wukong took a close look and said: 'Fool, that's Master being hung on the tree by bandits. You stay back, let me go check first.' The Great Sage transformed with a shake of his body, becoming a little monk carrying a blue cloth bundle, and walked forward.

[P7] 9 Wukong walked up to Tang Sanzang. The bandits surrounded him and said: 'Little monk, your master said the silver is in your pack. Take it out quickly, and we'll spare your lives!'
10 Wukong put down his pack and said: 'Your Majesty, don't shout. There's only a hundred or so taels of silver, but I have dozens of ingots of gold. Just let my master down first, and I'll give you the whole pack.' The bandit chief, upon hearing this, ordered his men to lower Tang Sanzang.

[P8] 11 Wukong pointed toward the path they came from and said to Tang僧: 'Master, go first. I'll catch up with you after I hand over the silver.' Tang僧 mounted his horse and rode away.
12 Wukong, seeing his master had gone far, spread out his pack and said: 'Bring it over!' The bandit chief hurriedly asked: 'What is it?' Wukong replied: 'Silver. I've carried an empty pack all this way. Give me some of the silver you stole to cover my expenses!'

[P9] 13 The bandit leader, furious, jumped up and swung a vine stick at Wukong's head, hitting him dozens of times in a row. He grew tired, his arms aching and hands sore, but Wukong merely flipped his eyes and laughed, saying, 'Come on, a few more hits! It's ticklish and actually quite pleasant.'
14 The bandits, unaware of Wukong's power, each grabbed their knives and spears and charged at him. Wukong, enraged, pulled out his golden cudgel, swung it left and right, and sent the two bandit leaders flying into the air, scaring all the henchmen into fleeing.

[P10] 15 At this moment, Tang Sanzang, Zhu Bajie, and Sha Wujing walked over. Tang Sanzang asked, 'Where did the bandits go?' Wukong replied, 'The henchmen have scattered. One of the two bandit leaders was thrown into the North Sea, and the other was sent to the South Mountain.'
16 That evening, the Tang Sanzang's disciples arrived at a village to ask for lodging. An old man surnamed Yang warmly invited them into his home.

[P11] 17 In the middle of the night, Tang Sanzang and his disciples were sleeping soundly when a group of bandits suddenly broke in. These were the very bandits who had been scattered in the pine forest earlier. Among them was the son of Old Man Yang. Upon seeing Tang Sanzang and his disciples staying there, they hurriedly sharpened their knives and cleaned their guns, intending to kill them.
18 Old Man Yang was a kind-hearted man who hated these bandits for their idle and wicked ways, but he couldn't discipline his own son. Seeing this situation, Old Man Yang quietly rushed to warn Tang Sanzang and led them to escape through the back door.

[P12] 19 The Tang Monk and his disciples had not gone far when they heard shouting from behind. The Tang Monk turned back and cried, “Oh no, the bandits are chasing us! What shall we do?!”
20 Wukong said to Bajie and Sha Wujing, “You two protect the Master and go first. I’ll deal with them!” The Tang Monk, worried, replied, “Wukong! Just scare them off, don’t hurt anyone again.”

[P13] 21 The bandits, wanting to commit violence under cover of darkness, chased after him and attacked Wukong wildly. To defend himself, Wukong swung his staff once, killing those bandits close to him, while the ones farther away fled in panic.
22 Seeing Wukong kill another person, Tang Sanzang scolded, 'You rascal, chasing them away was enough—why did you have to kill them!' As he spoke, he dismounted, sat down, and darkened his face, beginning to chant the Tightening Spell. The spell made Wukong's eyes swell and his head throb, causing him to roll on the ground in pain, while Tang Sanzang continued chanting without stopping.

[P14] 23 Wukong pleaded: 'Master, spare me! Don't chant it anymore!' Tang Sanzang finally stopped, saying: 'There's no point. I don't want you anymore. Go back!' 
24 Wukong knelt down and said: 'Master, why are you driving me away again?' Tang Sanzang said: 'You rascal, you're too vicious. You're not fit to be a pilgrim. Go! Go! Don't make me chant the true words again.' Wukong, angry, said 'Go!' and with a single somersault, vanished without a trace.

[P15] 25 Wukong thought to himself in the air: 'This monk has turned ungrateful. Why don't I go tell Guanyin Bodhisattva?' With that, he flew straight toward the South Sea.
26 Wukong arrived at珞伽 Mountain, passed through the Purple Bamboo Grove, rushed to the Cave of the Tides, bowed before Guanyin Bodhisattva, and wept bitterly, his tears flowing like a spring.

[P16] 27 The Bodhisattva learned the cause and said to Wukong: 'You should advise the bandits with kind words; killing them recklessly is also your fault.' Wukong felt unjustly treated and thought: Why is the Bodhisattva also so unfair, not distinguishing right from wrong?
28 Wukong begged the Bodhisattva to remove the Tightening咒 and let him return to the mountain. The Bodhisattva said: 'Protecting Master Tang on his journey to fetch the scriptures is the right path. The road to the West is full of dangers. Your master will come to find you. Stay here and wait.'

[P17] 29 After Tang Sanzang had sent Wukong away, he continued westward. After walking for half a day without seeing a village, he became hungry and thirsty. He sent Baijie to beg for food and water. When Baijie did not return after a long time, he sent Sha Wujing to look for him.
30 Tang Sanzang had just calmed his mind and closed his eyes to rest when he heard a gust of wind from the sky. He thought Baijie had returned. Opening his eyes, he saw Wukong holding a bowl of clear water standing before him.

[P18] 31 Wukong said: 'Master, without me, you won't even be able to get a drink of water, let alone reach the Western Heaven. Drink this water first, and I'll go for alms.' Tang僧 shouted: 'I'd rather die of thirst than drink your water! Go quickly, and don't slow down, or I'll chant the spell!' 
32 Wukong, upon hearing this, cursed angrily: 'You bald monk, you've wronged me too much!' Saying this, he swung his staff directly at Tang僧's back.

[P19] 33 Master Tang cried out in pain and fainted to the ground. Wukong paid no attention, grabbed the luggage, and flew away.
34 Soon after, Bajie and Sha僧 returned from foraging, saw their master lying on the ground, the white horse unbridled, and the luggage gone, and were greatly shocked.

[P20] 35 Sha Wujing lifted up his master and wept bitterly. Zhu Bajie said: 'This must be the doing of those bandits we didn't kill completely. Crying now is useless! You stay here with the body. I'll go sell the horse, buy a coffin, bury the master, then you go back to the Flowing Sand River, and I'll return to my Gao Family Village.'
36 Sha Wujing couldn't bear to leave, so he hurriedly told Zhu Bajie to give the master some water. Tang Sanzang swallowed a few mouthfuls, slowly regained consciousness, and told Zhu Bajie and Sha Wujing what had just happened. Zhu Bajie, furious and grinding his teeth, shouted: 'You rascal monkey, how dare you beat and insult the master! I'll go find you and settle this!'

[P21] 37 Sha Wujing grabbed Zhu Bajie and said, 'Don't rush. First, help Master to the village behind the mountain, get some hot soup for him to eat, find a place to stay, let him rest and recover. Then you can go after him.'
38 Zhu Bajie had no choice but to obey Sha Wujing, helping Master into the village to beg for some vegetarian food and hot soup. After eating half a bowl, Tang Sanzang felt a bit better and asked, 'Who will go to retrieve our luggage?'

[P22] 39 Pigsy wanted to go, but Tang Sanzang thought for a moment and said: 'You can't go. You've never gotten along with that monkey, and you speak rudely. If you anger him, even if you fight, you won't be able to beat him. Let Wujing go instead.'
40 As Sha Wujing was about to leave, Tang Sanzang repeatedly instructed: 'When you get there, act according to the situation. If he gives it to you, take it; if not, go to the Bodhisattva and report it. Under no circumstances should you argue or fight with him, because you are not his match!' Sha Wujing nodded in agreement, jumped onto the cloud, and headed for Dongsheng神州.

[P23] 41 Sha Wujing traveled for three days and three nights, crossed the Eastern Ocean, reached the Flower-Fruit Mountain region, landed from the clouds, found the Water Curtain Cave, and heard the monkeys chattering noisily.
42 Upon closer look, Sun Wukong was sitting high on a stone platform, shaking his head and swaying his brain as he recited the 'Passport Document'.

[P24] 43 Sha Wujing, hearing him recite halfway through about having taken in his elder brother Sun Wukong, his second brother... couldn't help but shout: "Elder brother, you stole the pass documents! You've prevented our master from going to the West to fetch the scriptures. Hurry and return them—our master is in great distress..."
44 Sun Wukong roared: "Who are you? How dare you intrude into my fairy cave!" Sha Wujing, seeing him turn his back and deny recognition, hurriedly bowed and said: "Elder brother, please calm down. Our master wronged you. If you don't bear a grudge against our master, please return with me. If not, at least return the luggage and pass documents to your younger brother..."

[P25] 45 Wukong coldly laughed: 'I hit Tang Sanzang and took the luggage because I want to go to the West to worship Buddha and fetch the scriptures, then deliver them to the Eastern Land. I will succeed alone, and have the people of Nanzhanbu Zhou establish me as their ancestor, famed for generations!' 
46 While Sha Wujing was stunned, Wukong said: 'Don't you believe me? Let me bring my Tang Sanzang for you to see.' At his shout, indeed, Tang Sanzang emerged from the cave riding the white horse, followed by Zhu Bajie carrying the luggage and Sha Wujing holding his staff.

[P26] 47 Sha Wujing, seeing this, became furious and shouted: 'I, Old Sha, don't change my name or surname. How can there be another Sha Monk? Evil spirit, don't run—take this!' He swung his staff, and with a single blow, the fake Sha Wujing revealed his true form—it was a monkey spirit in disguise.
48 The fake Wukong, enraged, ordered the monkeys to surround Sha Wujing and attack. Sha Wujing leaped into the air, mounted the clouds, and flew straight to the South Sea to report to the Bodhisattva.

[P27] 49 Sha Wujing arrived at珞伽 Mountain, paid respects to Guanyin Bodhisattva, and looked up to see Wukong standing beside her with a grin, which made him pause in surprise. He thought to himself: 'This rascal, standing before me, must have already twisted the truth in front of the Bodhisattva...'
50 As the Bodhisattva was about to ask questions, she saw Sha Wujing with furrowed brows and glaring eyes, raising his staff and striking at Wukong. Wukong dodged, and Sha Wujing chased after him. The Bodhisattva shouted: 'Wujing, stop! Speak clearly—why are you fighting in front of me?'

[P28] 51 Sha Wujing hurriedly apologized, then recounted the entire story, finally saying angrily: 'I came specially to report to the Bodhisattva, but I didn't expect him to arrive before me. I hope the Bodhisattva won't believe his lies!' 
52 The Bodhisattva said: 'Wujing, don't accuse others falsely. Wukong has been here for four days already.' Sha Wujing didn't believe it, pointing at Wukong and shouting: 'He is elusive and can change forms at will. I would never lie to the Bodhisattva!'

[P29] 53 The Bodhisattva saw Sha Wujing was so angry that his face turned red. She said, 'If that's the case, don't be angry. Call Wukong and go to Flower-Fruit Mountain together. You'll see for yourselves there.'
54 Wukong and Sha Wujing bid farewell to the Bodhisattva and left the cave. Sha Wujing grabbed Wukong and said, 'This time, we must go together. Don't hide and peek anymore.' Wukong agreed, and the two flew away on the clouds together.

[P30] 55 Upon arriving at Flower-Fruit Mountain, Sha Wujing first saw that 'Sun Wukong' and pointed to Wukong: 'Brother, look, who is sitting on that stone platform?!'
56 Wukong, seeing this, became furious and leaped forward, shouting: 'Where did you come from, demon! How dare you change my appearance, occupy my immortal cave, deceive my descendants, and take a strike from me!'

[P31] 57 The other Wukong didn't reply, but raised his staff to meet him. The two golden-hooped rods clashed up and down, their martial arts equally skilled, making it impossible to tell who was who.
58 It left Sha Wujing unable to tell which was real. He called out, 'Elder Brother!' and both answered at once. He wanted to help, but feared hurting the real one. Just as he was puzzled, one of them called out, 'Sha Wujing, go back first and report to the Master. I'll fight this demon all the way to Bodhisattva to prove who is real.'

[P32] 59 Sha Wujing listened and decided this one was the real one. But then the other one repeated everything word for word, and immediately confused him again. Sha Wujing thought: I can't help, I'll go get the luggage first.
60 But when he ran back to the cave entrance, he couldn't find the luggage. At this time, the two Wukongs had fought to an unknown destination, so he had no choice but to leave Flower-Fruit Mountain and return to report to his master.

[P33] 61 The two Wukongs fought all the way to珞伽 Mountain and met Guanyin Bodhisattva. One said, 'I am the real one.' The other said, 'He is the fake.' They argued endlessly.
62 The Bodhisattva couldn't tell which was real. She thought: I'll secretly chant the Tightening咒, and whoever feels pain is the real one. Unexpectly, as soon as she chanted, both clutched their heads and rolled on the ground, crying out in pain, 'Mercy!'

[P34] 63 The spell didn't work. The Bodhisattva called out to Wukong, and both answered. The Bodhisattva said: 'One of you must be fake. You've followed your master for years; go quickly and ask him to tell the truth.'
64 Meanwhile, Sha Wujing returned from Flower-Fruit Mountain and told his master. Tang Sanzang, regretful and fearful, said: 'I wronged Wukong. But this demon is immensely powerful. What if even Wukong cannot defeat him? If we lose our documents and luggage, how can we go to the West to fetch the scriptures?'

[P35] 65 The master and his three disciples were discussing when they heard a commotion in the sky. They hurried out to look and saw two Wukongs fighting and arguing as they came.
66 Bajie couldn't wait for them to land, so he leapt up and shouted, 'Let me, Old Pig, go check which monkey is the real one.'

[P36] 67 Pigsy arrived in the air, called out to his elder brother, and both answered together: 'Brother, you've come just in time, quickly help me fight the demon!' Pigsy looked at one, then the other, unable to tell which was real, and stepped forward, grabbing one by the arm and said: 'Come, let's go see Master.'
68 The monk saw the two Wukongs and couldn't tell which was real; even chanting the spell had no effect. Later, he came up with an idea and said: 'Wukong can transform seventy-two ways. Whatever I say, whoever can change into it is the real one.'

[P37] 69 The monk said, "Rooster!" In the blink of an eye, two identical big roosters appeared before them, stretching their necks and crowing.
70 The monk said, "Cricket!" In another blink of an eye, a pair of crickets of the same size appeared before them, fighting fiercely with their antennae.

[P38] 71 What are they saying? They can turn into anything. Frustrated, Tang僧 said, 'Whoever dares to go to the Temple of Thunder and meet Buddha, is the real one.' Hearing this, the two Wukongs pulled and tugged at each other, riding clouds and mist, and truly flew off to the Western Heaven.
72 After the two Wukongs left, Tang僧 hurriedly instructed Bajie: 'While he's not at Flower-Fruit Mountain, quickly go retrieve our luggage. Then we can continue our journey. No matter who is real or fake, I don't really expect to use him anymore.'

[P39] 73 It was said that Buddha was preaching when two Wukongs ran up, both asking him to distinguish the real from the fake. Buddha looked carefully and pointed at the fake Wukong, saying, 'You bold Six-Eared Macaque, how dare you deceive me all the way here.'
74 The fake Wukong, upon hearing Buddha reveal his true identity, was terrified and trembled with fear. Just as he tried to flee, he was already surrounded by the gods.

[P40] 75 The fake Wukong hurriedly shook his body, transformed into a bee to escape, but was caught in Buddha's golden bowl and immediately revealed his true form.
76 Wukong, unable to contain his rage, struck down with his staff and ended the life of the Six-Eared Macaque.

[P41] 77 At this moment, the Bodhisattva arrived. The Buddha said that protecting Tang Sanzang on his journey to the West to obtain scriptures was the right path, and instructed the Bodhisattva to take Wukong to see Tang Sanzang.
78 Wukong followed the Bodhisattva to meet Tang Sanzang, cleared up the misunderstanding, and the master and disciples reconciled as before. Just then, Bajie also returned from Flower-Fruit Mountain, carrying the luggage. The Bodhisattva returned to the South Sea, and the four disciples of Tang Sanzang happily resumed their journey westward. To learn what happens next, please read 'The Three Theft of the Banana Fan'.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为《西游记》连环画第廿一章的封面，标题为《真假孙悟空》，画面描绘了两个孙悟空在云端激烈对战的场景。
[P2] 本页为《真假孙悟空》连环画的封面及内容提要，介绍了该画册改编自《西游记》第五十六至五十八回，讲述了孙悟空被师父驱逐后，六耳猕猴冒充悟空抢走行李，最终在如来帮助下真相大白、师徒重归于好的故事梗概。
[P3] 唐僧师徒西行途中，一群小猴从山中跑出，模仿孙悟空和同伴们的动作，并跳上白龙马乱抓乱挠，惹得八戒大笑，称它们是孙悟空的子孙后代。
[P4] 唐僧骑马出山口后马受惊狂奔，多亏松林阻挡才得以控制。稍作喘息后，一群强盗从松林中冲出，拦路索要买路钱，威胁要让唐僧‘秃头搬家’。
[P5] 唐僧被强盗拦路，他哀求无果后谎称银子在徒弟身上，结果被强盗绑起来吊在树上。
[P6] 孙悟空和猪八戒赶到被强盗劫持的唐僧处，八戒远远看到师父在树上，悟空则识破是师父被吊在树上，便化身为小和尚前去探查。
[P7] 孙悟空化装成小和尚接近强盗，谎称银子在包袱里，要求先放师父下来才交出财物，强盗头目同意后命人放下了唐僧。
[P8] 孙悟空让唐僧先走，自己则假装交出银子，实则用空包袱骗强盗，要求分些劫来的银子作为盘缠。
[P9] 孙悟空被强盗头目用藤棍猛打，却毫不在意；随后强盗们一拥而上，悟空取出金箍棒，将两个贼头甩飞，吓跑所有喽啰。
[P10] 孙悟空打败强盗后，向唐僧汇报战果，称已将贼首扔进北海和南山；当晚，师徒四人抵达一村庄，被姓杨的老汉热情收留借宿。
[P11] 半夜，曾被孙悟空打散的强盗闯入杨老汉家，欲杀害唐僧师徒；杨老汉见状，悄悄通知唐僧并带他们从后门逃走。
[P12] 唐僧师徒刚离开村庄不久，便听到身后有强盗追来，唐僧惊慌失措；孙悟空让八戒和沙僧保护师父先走，自己留下对付强盗，唐僧则叮嘱他不要伤人。
[P13] 强盗追上孙悟空并围攻，孙悟空自卫将其击毙；唐僧见状责骂并念紧箍咒，导致孙悟空痛苦不堪。
[P14] 孙悟空因被唐僧念紧箍咒而痛苦哀求，唐僧最终赶他离开；孙悟空跪地质问，唐僧斥其凶恶，孙悟空生气后一个筋斗消失不见。
[P15] 孙悟空被唐僧赶走后，心生委屈，决定前往南海找观音菩萨诉苦。他飞到落伽山，穿过紫竹林，在潮音洞前拜见观音，痛哭流涕。
[P16] 孙悟空向观音菩萨诉苦，菩萨劝他应以劝诫代替杀戮，悟空心生不平；随后悟空请求解除紧箍咒，菩萨劝他等待师父来寻，并让他暂住此处。
[P17] 唐僧在赶走孙悟空后继续西行，因饥饿口渴派八戒取水，久等未归又派沙僧寻找；正当他闭目养神时，孙悟空突然出现，捧着一盂清水站在他面前。
[P18] 孙悟空为唐僧取水归来，唐僧拒绝饮用并威胁要念紧箍咒，孙悟空愤怒之下挥棒击向唐僧后背。
[P19] 孙悟空挥棒击中唐僧后背，唐僧晕倒在地，孙悟空提着行李驾云离开；不久后，猪八戒和沙僧化斋归来，发现师父倒地、白马脱缰、行李不见，十分震惊。
[P20] 猪八戒和沙僧发现唐僧倒地后，八戒认为是强盗所为并打算卖马买棺材，沙僧不忍离弃；唐僧苏醒后讲述被孙悟空打骂的经过，八戒愤怒地发誓要找孙悟空算账。
[P21] 沙僧劝阻八戒急于找孙悟空报仇，先扶唐僧到村庄休息调养；八戒无奈依从，唐僧吃下斋饭后稍有精神，询问谁去取回行李。
[P22] 唐僧拒绝让猪八戒去找孙悟空取行李，认为他不是对手，改派沙僧前往，并叮嘱他见机行事，若孙悟空不给就去菩萨处告状。沙僧答应后驾云出发。
[P23] 沙僧历经三天三夜抵达花果山，发现孙悟空正坐在水帘洞的石台上念着通关文牒。
[P24] 沙僧抵达花果山，发现孙悟空正在念通关文牒，急忙上前指责其偷走关文；孙悟空怒斥沙僧闯入仙洞，沙僧连忙行礼，请求他归还行李和关文或一同回师。
[P25] 孙悟空向沙僧解释自己打唐僧、抢行李是为了独自取经成名，并当场召唤出唐僧、八戒和沙僧的幻象以证明自己的说法。
[P26] 沙僧识破假沙僧的真身，将其打回原形；假悟空恼羞成怒，命众猴围攻，沙僧跳上云头，前往南海向菩萨告状。
[P27] 沙僧抵达落伽山向观音菩萨告状，发现孙悟空已在场，怀疑他先说了谎；沙僧愤怒地举杖欲打孙悟空，被菩萨喝止。
[P28] 沙僧向观音菩萨告状，称孙悟空先到并撒谎；菩萨指出孙悟空已在此住四天，沙僧不信并坚持自己没有说谎。
[P29] 观音菩萨见沙僧愤怒，提议让孙悟空与沙僧一同前往花果山查明真相；二人辞别菩萨后，沙僧拉住孙悟空，要求他不再躲藏，两人一同驾云前往花果山。
[P30] 沙僧和孙悟空一同来到花果山，沙僧发现一个假冒的孙悟空坐在石台上，便指给真孙悟空看；真孙悟空怒斥假悟空冒充自己、占据仙洞，并准备出手教训。
[P31] 真孙悟空与假孙悟空在花果山展开激烈打斗，两人武艺相当，难分胜负；沙僧在旁无法分辨真假，正犹豫是否出手相助时，其中一个孙悟空提议让沙僧先回唐僧处禀报，自己则与假悟空前往南海菩萨处辨明真伪。
[P32] 沙僧在花果山被两个孙悟空的言行弄得无法分辨真假，决定先去取行李，但返回后发现行李不见，两个孙悟空也已打散，他只好独自离开花果山，回唐僧处禀报。
[P33] 两个孙悟空打到落伽山，向观音菩萨争辩真假，菩萨无法分辨，便暗念紧箍咒，结果两人同时喊疼，无法判断真伪。
[P34] 观音菩萨无法用紧箍咒分辨真假孙悟空，便让二人去找唐僧辨认；沙僧回到唐僧处，唐僧后悔错怪孙悟空，担心妖怪强大，若悟空斗不过会丢失行李，无法西天取经。
[P35] 师徒三人正在议论时，两个孙悟空打闹着从空中飞来；猪八戒见状，跃起声称要亲自去辨认真假。
[P36] 猪八戒赶到空中，两个孙悟空都称他为兄弟并请求他帮忙打妖精，猪八戒无法分辨真假，便拉住其中一个去见师父；唐僧见到两个孙悟空也无法分辨，念咒无效，于是想出办法，让两人根据他说的话进行变化，以辨明真伪。
[P37] 唐僧让两个孙悟空分别变化成公鸡和蟋蟀，以辨明真伪，两人变化后形态完全相同，无法分辨。
[P38] 唐僧让两个孙悟空去雷音寺见如来佛辨明真伪，两人随即驾云前往；唐僧则吩咐猪八戒趁机去花果山找回行李，表示不再指望孙悟空。
[P39] 两个孙悟空来到雷音寺求如来辨认真假，如来识破假悟空是六耳猕猴，假悟空惊慌欲逃，被众神围住。
[P40] 假悟空试图化作蜜蜂逃跑，被如来用金钵罩住现出原形；真悟空怒不可遏，一棒打死六耳猕猴。
[P41] 如来佛祖派菩萨带孙悟空去见唐僧，师徒二人和好如初；猪八戒也从花果山带回行李，四人重新踏上西行之路。
